answer: The paper charges dGSLM with three limitations: it does not run in an online fashion, it does not benefit from the knowledge of a text language model, and it does not model acoustic information as it only models semantic tokens [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 6]. Moshi addresses these by modeling two streams of semantic and acoustic tokens hierarchically, allowing it to be full-duplex and exploit all available information [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 6].
question: dGSLM was already full-duplex. Which three limits does the paper still charge it with, and what does Moshi do differently?
